glossary.definition: A Ping release claim (2026-11-02), listing and cap measured on gateway v1.261106 (2026-11-08), per-caller entitlement UNVERIFIED on our tenant, and simulated in this app: an aggregate of member MCP servers has one policy that caps what any member tool may be used for. It is enforced on the listing and again at the member hop. The cap only removes: a tool the member itself denies stays denied. The console API has no field for it, so this lab gives it no field name.

A Ping release claim (2026-11-02), listing and cap measured on gateway v1.261106 (2026-11-08), per-caller entitlement UNVERIFIED on our tenant, and simulated in this app: a tool the caller is not entitled to is removed from tools/list instead of only being refused when called, and it is refused again when called by name. The simulation is lab-invented; the console API has no field for it.

A scan of an entitlement-filtered list covers only what that caller sees. A tool hidden from this caller was never scanned, so a clean result is not a clean result for any other caller. The scan notes and the Limits page say so.
Text in tool metadata written for the model rather than the person: an instruction tag, an order to keep something from the user, or an imperative aimed at the agent.

An application of type mcp-aggregate that merges several member MCP servers into one. Console swagger names, 2026-10-31, schema only: Members, and per member AppRef, Alias and ToolFilter. The schema says a member's tools are namespaced as Alias__tool. These names already existed on 2026-10-26; the behaviour is a Ping claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant.

The machine-readable result of a scan (scan-report/1): the findings with rule id, severity and evidence, the input counts, the rule table and the list of what a metadata scan cannot catch. It records enforcement as none.

Console swagger name, 2026-10-31, schema only: a string array on each aggregate member. The schema gives the name and type and nothing about meaning. This lab reads it as the allow-list of that member's tools the aggregate exposes; that reading is the lab's.
What a server says about its tools: names, descriptions and input schemas. An agent reads it as trusted context before it ever calls a tool.
Putting instructions or traps in tool metadata. The model reads that text as trusted context and the person normally never sees it.

glossary.term: Why it matters: MCP aggregate (Ping claims)
glossary.definition: Ping claims from its H2 2026 deck (slide 37), UNVERIFIED on our tenant. Challenge: each agent-server pair needs its own connection, configuration and credential, so effort and attack surface grow with each pair. Technical: one connection, one policy cap enforced twice, one audit trail across members. Business: new servers join by configuration, not project work, for a lower per-integration cost and a faster rollout.

glossary.term: Why it matters: MCP gateway (Ping claims)
glossary.definition: Ping claims from its H2 2026 deck (slide 36), UNVERIFIED on our tenant. Challenge: one shared token and every tool exposed to every caller means no attribution and no per-tool control, so security stalls adoption. Technical: per-user identity, per-tool policy and injected credentials on every call, fully audited. Business: MCP integrations proceed under existing governance, with faster time to value on agent projects.

cards.label: Entitled listing and aggregate cap (Ping release claim)
cards.description: A Ping release claim (2026-11-02), listing and cap measured on gateway v1.261106 (2026-11-08), per-caller entitlement UNVERIFIED on our tenant: tools a caller may not use are removed from the list and refused by name, and an aggregate policy cap is enforced twice. Mock simulates it and lets you edit the policy; Real measures your own gateway's aggregate apps with your agent keys.

cards.label: What a scan cannot catch
cards.description: Result injection, rug-pulls after the scan, unfetched content and novel phrasing.

cards.label: Scan this listing as each caller
cards.description: The scan reads the list exactly as one caller sees it. A clean result is clean for that caller only.

cards.label: The six checks a tool must pass
cards.description: The tool exists, its member is reachable, the caller signed in to it, the ToolFilter exposes it, the member policy allows the caller, the aggregate cap allows it. The check that stopped a call is highlighted.

cards.label: Story: only what you may see
cards.description: Same server, different callers: what each is shown, what is refused by name, what the cap removes, and what a scan of a filtered list cannot say.

cards.label: Try this: six guided steps
cards.description: One click sets the caller, the view and the call: Guest sees one tool, the cap refuses a call, the ToolFilter refuses a call, a member used directly skips the cap, the member says no, a member goes down.

stories.title: An operator sees only what An operator may use
stories.say: A tool you were never shown should also be a tool you cannot call. The release says so; this lab only shows the shape.
